FINDING_ID: Codex_R5_DR_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: The founder-locked ascending-abstraction guard is not enforced. `_abstraction_dropping()` exists, but `stop()` never uses it; the actual predicate is just `(smoothed_mu < tau_mu) or (smoothed_novelty < tau_novelty_stop) or vocab_saturated`. That means the detector can stop even while the remaining findings are becoming more abstract and system-level valuable, which contradicts both the class contract and the in-code design notes.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make the abstraction guard part of the executable predicate, not just documentation. If the intended rule is conjunctive, wire `self._abstraction_dropping(round_idx)` directly into `stop()` and add tests showing that low `mu` alone does not stop when abstraction is still rising.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R5_DR_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: Phase D “per-area” vocabulary tracking is keyed by `str(f.flaw_class)`, which is not an area identifier. In the supplied findings corpus, the same `FLAW_CLASS` values appear across multiple architectural areas, so this code merges unrelated areas into one vocabulary bucket and splits one area across multiple buckets when its findings span multiple flaw classes. That breaks the stated guarantee that stop fires only when all active areas are saturated.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require a real `area_id` or `module_id` on `Finding`, or pass the reviewed area explicitly into `add_round_from_findings()`. Do not enable Phase D per-area saturation from `flaw_class` proxies.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R5_DR_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: `add_model_round()` treats every finding produced by a model as fresh yield: `len(findings) * mean(abstraction)`, accumulated cumulatively. There is no deduplication against that model’s prior output or the system’s prior findings. A model can therefore keep `per_model_mu()` positive by repeating old findings, or by “rediscovering” another model’s earlier finding, even when true marginal system value is already exhausted. Because `smoothed_marginal_value()` prefers per-model aggregation when present, this can materially delay stopping.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base per-model yield on globally novel contributions or equivalence-class deltas, not raw emitted findings. Maintain seen-signatures/classes and only credit a model for new system value it actually adds.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R5_DR_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The backward-compatibility switch for per-model mode is too coarse. `smoothed_marginal_value()` changes behavior for all rounds as soon as `_per_model_yields` is merely non-empty. That means one partially instrumented model or one partially recorded round silently disables system-level `mu` for the whole smoothing window, producing decisions from incomplete per-model coverage.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Decide aggregation mode per round, not globally. Only use per-model aggregation when coverage is complete for the active/dispatched models in that round; otherwise fall back to system-level `mu` or raise an explicit completeness error.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R5_DR_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: Zero-cost positive-yield rounds are documented as maximally valuable (`inf`), but the aggregation path throws that information away. Both `aggregate_per_model_mu()` and `smoothed_marginal_value()` filter with `math.isfinite`, so an `inf` round is excluded rather than propagated. In the extreme case where all current value is “free,” aggregation falls back to `0.0`, which can trigger a false stop and directly contradicts the detector’s own rule.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Preserve positive infinity through aggregation and smoothing. If any contributing round/model has `mu = inf`, return `inf` for that aggregate/window instead of dropping it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R5_DR_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: [CROSS-COMPONENT, UNVERIFIED FROM THIS SCOPE] System-level `marginal_value()` assumes contiguous iterative indices and uses only `round_idx - 1` as the predecessor, while `per_model_mu()` already searches backward for the most recent prior round. If the orchestrator emits sparse/reused indices or phase-boundary index reuse, system-level `mu` will compare against `0.0` instead of the last observed yield. Existing FSM findings already suggest round-index ambiguity, so this hidden assumption is risky.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either validate contiguous iterative indices when rounds are recorded, or make `marginal_value()` use the same “most recent prior round” lookup that `per_model_mu()` already uses.  
VERIFIED: FALSE
